definitions.explanation: Refers to expressions, phrases, or usages that have become established through long custom and repeated use, even if they may not follow strict grammatical or semantic rules.

examples.japanese: {慣用|かんよう}{句|く}を{覚|おぼ}える。
これは{慣用|かんよう}{的|てき}な{言|い}い{方|かた}だ。
examples.english: This is an idiomatic way of saying it.

examples.japanese: 「{的|まと}を{射|い}る」は{正|ただ}しい{慣用|かんよう}{表現|ひょうげん}だが、「{的|まと}を{得|え}る」も{広|ひろ}く{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: "Mato o iru" is the correct idiomatic expression, but "mato o eru" is also widely used.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly seen in the compound {慣用|かんよう}{句|く} (idiomatic phrase/idiom). Also used as a no-adjective ({慣用|かんよう}の) or with ～{的|てき} ({慣用|かんよう}{的|てき}). In linguistics, {慣用|かんよう}{読|よ}み refers to a customary reading of kanji that differs from the standard reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣用|かんよう}{句|く}: idiomatic expression, idiom
- {慣用|かんよう}{表現|ひょうげん}: idiomatic expression
- {慣用|かんよう}{読|よ}み: customary reading (of kanji)
- {慣用|かんよう}{的|てき}: idiomatic, conventional
